{{nihongo|'''Idate Shrine'''|伊達神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mutsu Province]].

'''Idate Shrine'''（いだてじんじゃ）is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Shikama, Miyagi|arz|شيكاما|ceb|Shikama-cho|es|Shikama (Miyagi)|fa|شیکاما، میاگی|fr|Shikama|id|Shikama, Miyagi|it|Shikama|ja|色麻町|ko|시카마정|ms|Shikama, Miyagi|my|ရှိခမမြို့၊ မိယဂိ|pl|Shikama|ru|Сикама|tl|Shikama, Miyagi|tr|Shikama|uk|Сікама (Міяґі)|ur|شیکاما، میاگی|uz|Shikama (Miyagi)|zh|色麻町|zh_yue|色麻町|qid=Q1204478}}, {{ill|Kami District, Miyagi|ceb|Kami-gun|fr|District de Kami|id|Distrik Kami, Miyagi|it|Distretto di Kami|ja|加美郡|ko|가미군|pl|Powiat Kami (Miyagi)|ru|Ками (уезд)|uk|Повіт Камі|zh|加美郡|zh_yue|加美郡|qid=Q1155600}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|Q47896|qid=Q47896}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}), and its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}} was {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}. It stands on the round tumulus called Oyama Kofun on the left bank of the Hana River, a tributary of the {{ill|Naruse River|arz|نهر ناروس|fa|رود ناروس|ja|鳴瀬川|ru|Нарусе|qid=Q11675397}}.

== History ==
Tradition says it was enshrined in the Enryaku era (782-806) when {{ill|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|bn|সাকানোউয়ে নো তামারামারো|ca|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|de|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|el|Σακανόουε νο Ταμουραμάρο|es|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|eu|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|fa|ساکانواوئه نو تامورامارو|fr|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|it|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|ja|坂上田村麻呂|ko|사카노우에노 다무라마로|pl|Tamuramaro Sakanoue|pt|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|ru|Саканоуэ-но Тамурамаро|simple|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|sl|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|tr|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|uk|Саканоуе но Тамурамаро|vi|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|zh|坂上田村麻呂|zh_classical|坂上田村麻呂|zh_min_nan|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|qid=Q941979}} campaigned east. Another tradition says people from around Ikashi District of {{ill|Harima Province|Q1047523|qid=Q1047523}} settled here and enshrined Iyoshi Ōkami ({{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|ja|五十猛神|simple|Isotakeru-no-kami|zh|五十猛神|qid=Q10881556|lt=Isatake-no-Kami}}) from {{ill|Itatehyōzu Shrine|Q11458547|qid=Q11458547}} in Ikashi, Harima.

In the mid-Heian {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it appears as "Mutsu Province, Shikama District, Idate Shrine, myōjin taisha," indicating its listing as {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}.

When the {{ill|Date clan|Q1151061|qid=Q1151061}} became governor of Mutsu, the shrine became associated with them, and the name was changed to '''Katori-sha''' in reference to {{ill|Katori Jingū|Q372380|qid=Q372380}}, where one of this shrine's deities, {{ill|Futsunushi|fr|Futsunushi|it|Futsunushi|ja|経津主神|mni|ꯐꯨꯠꯁꯨꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Futsunushi|ru|Фуцунуси|zh|經津主神|qid=Q1107286|lt=Futsunushi}}, is enshrined. In 1872 (Meiji 5), the name was restored to "Idate Shrine."

== Shikama ancient three shrines ==
{{座標一覧|節=色麻古社三社}}
Together with this shrine, the following three are called the "three ancient shrines of Shikama":
* Idate Shrine - south of Naruse River
* {{ill|Shibagaki Shrine|ja|柴籬神社|qid=Q11534936|lt=Akatsuka Kashima Shrine}}（{{ill|Kami, Miyagi|Q1205414|qid=Q1205414}}Yokkaichiba Aza Yashiki, {{ウィキ座標|38|33|20.6|N|140|51|59.6|E|region:JP|地図|name=Akatsuka Kashima Shrine}}）- north of Naruse River
* Ukisu Shrine（Kami-shimo-shinden, {{ウィキ座標|38|32|38.6|N|140|52|31|E|region:JP|地図|name=Ukisu Shrine}}) - north of Naruse River

It is said that their triangular placement across the Naruse River was modeled after the "Three Shrines of the East": {{ill|Kashima Jingū|Q706499|qid=Q706499}} (Ichinomiya of {{ill|Hitachi Province|cs|Provincie Hitači|de|Provinz Hitachi|es|Provincia de Hitachi|fa|ولایت هیتاچی|fr|Province de Hitachi|gl|Provincia de Hitachi|hak|Hitachi-koet|id|Provinsi Hitachi|it|Hitachi (provincia)|ja|常陸国|ko|히타치국|lt|Hitačio žemė|nl|Hitachi (provincie)|pt|Província de Hitachi|ru|Хитати (провинция)|simple|Hitachi Province|sk|Hitači (provincia)|sr|Провинција Хитачи|tr|Hitachi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Хітаті|zh|常陸國|zh_min_nan|Hitati-kok|zh_yue|常陸國|qid=Q1055353}}), {{ill|Katori Jingū|Q372380|qid=Q372380}} (Ichinomiya of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|Q1053695|qid=Q1053695}}), and {{ill|Ikisu Shrine|Q11073095|qid=Q11073095}} in {{ill|Kamisu|Q840595|qid=Q840595}}, which form a triangle around the {{ill|Tone River|Q177452|qid=Q177452}}.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=Greeting|url=http://www.kashimajinja.org/m_aisatu.htm|publisher=Kashima Shrine|accessdate=2012-08-27}}</ref>
